# SecFn

> Encrypted secrets, scoped runtime retrieval, scanning, and audit services.

## Documentation

- [Audit and rate limits](https://secfn.com/docs/audit-and-rate-limits) — Configure durable security events and quota enforcement.
- [Getting started](https://secfn.com/docs/getting-started) — Choose the core, server, and runtime packages.
- [SecFn](https://secfn.com/docs) — Encrypted secrets, scoped retrieval, scanning, and security services.
- [Schema and migrations](https://secfn.com/docs/migrations) — Apply SecFn's schema and PostgreSQL changes in order.
- [Operations and limits](https://secfn.com/docs/operations-and-limits) — Key custody, adapter guarantees, and validation boundaries.
- [Core package](https://secfn.com/docs/reference/core) — Encryption, scanner, schema, and shared contracts.
- [Reference](https://secfn.com/docs/reference) — SecFn packages, routes, and source package guides.
- [Packages](https://secfn.com/docs/reference/packages) — Current SecFn package map and import surfaces.
- [Routes](https://secfn.com/docs/reference/routes) — SecFn admin and runtime route families.
- [Runtime package](https://secfn.com/docs/reference/runtime) — Read-only runtime client and environment materialization.
- [Server package](https://secfn.com/docs/reference/server) — Control plane, runtime API, migration, and storage contract.
- [Runtime client](https://secfn.com/docs/runtime) — Read secrets and materialize sets in trusted processes.
- [Secret scanning](https://secfn.com/docs/scanning) — Run the core scanner and persist run metadata through the server.
- [Scope and permissions](https://secfn.com/docs/scope-and-permissions) — Enforce tenant, namespace, environment, and operator boundaries.
- [Secrets and sets](https://secfn.com/docs/secrets-and-sets) — Create, rotate, reveal, and resolve versioned secrets safely.
- [Server setup](https://secfn.com/docs/server) — Configure persistence, encryption, host context, and route mounting.
